behavior_preservation: exact — str.split never returns an empty list, so the else arm is never taken; removing it (use `parts[-1]` unconditionally) preserves behavior identically.
title: archive_branch has an unreachable `else` fallback on `parts = branch.split('/')`
description: `parts = branch.split('/')` is then used as `archive_name = f"{_ARCHIVE_PREFIX}/{parts[-1]}" if parts else f"{_ARCHIVE_PREFIX}/{branch}"`. `str.split('/')` ALWAYS returns a non-empty list (e.g. `'x'.split('/') == ['x']`, `''.split('/') == ['']`), so `if parts` is unconditionally truthy and the `else` arm is dead code. Additionally, `branch` is non-empty here because `_validate_ref_name(branch)` (line 875) rejects empty names, so `parts[-1]` is always a real value. The ternary can be reduced to `archive_name = f"{_ARCHIVE_PREFIX}/{parts[-1]}"`.
evidence: Line 886-888. `branch.split('/')` cannot yield [] for any str input; `_validate_ref_name` already guarantees branch != ''. Hence the else branch is unreachable.
